items.title: DeepSeek Pushes Out Updated AI Model It Says Is Faster, Leaner
items.author: Saritha Rai
items.content: <article>DeepSeek released an update of its AI model this weekend that it says is faster and leaner, ramping up the Chinese company’s challenge to Silicon Valley rivals Anthropic PBC and OpenAI as well as domestic competitors like Moonshot Kimi and Z.ai</article>

items.title: AI Selloff Tests Investor Confidence
items.content: <article>Ritholtz Wealth Management Chairman and Chief Investment Officer Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that AI remains a transformational technology, but investors face a difficult task determining which companies will ultimately emerge as winners and losers. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz discusses CoreWeave’s selloff, concerns about AI financing and valuations, and the challenges facing Tesla as competition in electric vehicles intensifies. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Zelenskyy Says Starlink Speed Restrictions Look Deliberate
items.author: Olesia Safronova and Daryna Krasnolutska
items.content: <article>Restrictions on Ukraine’s military use of SpaceX’s Starlink system appear to be deliberate and not the result of any technical problems, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, while denouncing a US decision to waive sanctions against Russia.</article>

items.title: The EV Bust Creating a New Battery Boom
items.content: <article>Factories built to supply America’s electric-vehicle boom are getting a second life making batteries for the power grid.  As EV demand weakens and electricity demand from data centers and new factories strengthens, battery makers are shifting toward stationary storage, but the new market still relies on federal incentives and a supply chain that remains partly dependent on China. The shift is visible at TransGrid’s Atlas projects in Arizona, where the contractor Qcells is using LG Energy Solution’s US-made battery cells. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: David Byrne Explains How Forgotten Ideas Come Back to Life
items.content: <article>History is littered with ideas that have been tossed aside, only for them to gain relevance at some later date. Think of Moby-Dick: forgotten in Melville's time, but now regarded as the great American novel. Or the work of economist Hyman Minsky, which became influential a decade after his death, when the 2008 financial crisis made “the Minsky Moment” a mainstream term. These are just a couple of the things we talk about with the legendary musician David Byrne on today's podcast. Byrne's new book, Sleeping Beauties: Why Good Ideas Go Dormant and How They Wake Up, looks to categorize numerous “sleeping beauties” — ideas that were lost but then rediscovered. Besides Melville and Minsky, we also talk about the lost Roman recipe for concrete and we get into Byrne's thoughts on how to write a song and his own experience of having his music rediscovered by a new generation. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Arrested OpenAI Engineer Seeks Bail, Denies Planning to Flee
items.author: Peter Blumberg
items.content: <article>The OpenAI software engineer charged with using a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices asked to be freed from custody and denied his purchase of a one-way plane ticket to his native Saudi Arabia was part of a plan to flee US justice.</article>

items.title: Reliance Pushes Back After Musk Questioned Starlink India Delay
items.author: P R Sanjai
items.content: <article>Reliance Industries Ltd., led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, pushed back against suggestions that it is trying to keep Elon Musk’s Starlink Inc. out of India, saying its own satellite venture is still awaiting regulatory clearances.</article>

items.title: Nvidia Partner GMI Cloud Calls CoreWeave 15% Yield ‘Insane’
items.author: Aileen Chuang
items.content: <article>The founder of a cloud computing company with a similar business model to CoreWeave Inc. said the 15% yield on the latter’s bonds is “insane,” compared with the roughly 3.45% rate his company secured on a recent Taiwan dollar loan.</article>

items.title: AI Music Deals Are Happening, But How Artists Will Be Paid Remains a Mystery
items.author: Ashley Carman
items.content: <article>How exactly AI money will flow through the music industry remains ambiguous</article>
